# Quick Start

Get started with appenv in minutes.

## Creating a New Project

### Interactive Setup

```text
# Create and enter project directory
mkdir httpie && cd httpie

# Run bootstrap
curl -sL https://github.com/flyingcircusio/appenv/raw/master/bootstrap | sh
```

The bootstrap script will guide you through:

```
What should the command be named? [app] http
Enter dependencies (one per line, empty line to finish):
  Default: http
  Dependency: httpie
  Dependency: 
Project name [http-app]: http
Description []: HTTP CLI
Minimum Python version [3.10]: 3.14
```

### Generated Files

```
httpie/
├── pyproject.toml    # Dependencies and metadata
├── uv.lock           # Lockfile (generated by update-lockfile)
├── appenv            # Bootstrap script
├── http              # Symlink to appenv (entry point)
└── .appenv/
    └── venv/         # Virtual environment
```

## Bootstrapping a Project

Use the bootstrap script to create a new project:

```text
$ mkdir httpie && cd httpie
$ curl -sL https://github.com/flyingcircusio/appenv/raw/master/bootstrap | sh
Let's create a new pyproject.toml project.

What should the command be named? [app] http
Enter dependencies (one per line, empty line to finish):
  Default: http
  Dependency: httpie
  Dependency: 
Project name [http-app]: http
Description []: HTTP CLI
Minimum Python version [3.10]: 3.14

Created pyproject.toml
Created http symlink

Done. pyproject.toml created.

Generating lockfile ...
✓ Created (+273 lines)

Run `./http` to bootstrap and run

$ ./http
Installing httpie ...
http: warning: command-line flag syntax is deprecated
```

## Project Structure

appenv expects a `pyproject.toml` in your project directory:

```
myproject/
├── pyproject.toml    # Dependencies and metadata
├── uv.lock           # Lockfile (generated by update-lockfile)
├── appenv            # Bootstrap script
├── mycommand         # Symlink to appenv (entry point)
└── .appenv/
    ├── venv/         # Virtual environment
    ├── current -> venv  # Legacy symlink
    ├── logs/         # Rotating log files (prepare.log, develop.log, etc.)
    └── profiling/    # Profiling data
```

**Environment isolation:** appenv clears `PYTHONPATH` before running to ensure clean isolation from system packages.

## Running Your Application

```text
# First run - installs dependencies automatically
./http GET https://httpbin.org/get

# Subsequent runs are instant
./http GET https://httpbin.org/get
```

## Adding Dependencies with `uv add`

Use `./appenv uv add <package>` to add dependencies. This updates both `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` in one step:

```text
$ ./appenv uv add requests
Resolved 5 packages in 12ms
Prepared 1 package in 45ms
Installed 1 package in 23ms
  + requests==2.32.3
```

**What changed:**

`pyproject.toml` (before):
```toml
[project]
name = "http"
dependencies = ["httpie>=3.0.0"]
```

`pyproject.toml` (after):
```toml
[project]
name = "http"
dependencies = [
    "httpie>=3.0.0",
    "requests>=2.32.3",
]
```

`uv.lock` gets the resolved version with all transitive dependencies:
```toml
[[package]]
name = "requests"
version = "2.32.3"
source = { registry = "https://pypi.org/simple" }
dependencies = [
    { name = "certifi" },
    { name = "charset-normalizer" },
    { name = "idna" },
    { name = "urllib3" },
]
```

## Upgrading Packages

UV won't upgrade packages on new releases. To upgrade:

```text
# Upgrade specific package
$ ./appenv uv lock --upgrade-package requests

# Upgrade all packages (within version constraints)
$ ./appenv uv lock --upgrade
```

## Freezing dependencies for repeatable builds

Use `update-lockfile` to create a lockfile for reproducible installs:

```text
$ ./appenv update-lockfile
✓ Created (+42 lines)

$ time ./http GET https://httpbin.org/get
Installing httpie ...
./http GET https://httpbin.org/get  2.91s user 0.99s system 88% cpu 4.407 total

$ time ./http GET https://httpbin.org/get
./http GET https://httpbin.org/get  0.22s user 0.11s system 90% cpu 0.371 total
```

### Options

```text
$ ./appenv update-lockfile --diff     # Show changes without writing
$ ./appenv update-lockfile -v         # Show detailed output
```

## Python version selection

appenv reads `requires-python` from `pyproject.toml` and selects the best available Python that satisfies the constraint:

```toml
[project]
name = "myapp"
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
```

appenv will:
1. Find all Python versions in PATH
2. Select the newest one matching the constraint
3. Re-exec itself with that Python

If no matching Python is found, it exits with an error showing available versions.

See {doc}`locking-behavior` for UV universal resolution details.

## Migrating from requirements.txt

If you have an existing project with `requirements.txt`:

```text
$ ./appenv migrate
Migrating from requirements.txt to pyproject.toml...

Found 3 dependency(ies): requests, click, rich
warning: 1 editable install(s) skipped:
  -e ./lib

Created pyproject.toml
```

Editable installs (both local and remote) are skipped with a warning. They require manual configuration in `pyproject.toml` after migration.

The `requirements.txt` is kept as legacy. Delete it when migration is complete.

```text
$ ./appenv --help
usage: appenv <COMMAND>

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

Commands:
  Project:
    init              Create a new pyproject.toml project.
    migrate           Migrate from requirements.txt to pyproject.toml.
    update-lockfile   Update the lock file.

  Venv:
    develop           Prepare the venv with dev dependencies.
    prepare           Prepare the venv.
    reset             Reset the environment.

  Tools:
    python            Spawn the embedded Python interpreter REPL
    run               Run a script from the bin/ directory of the vir...
    uv                Run uv with the appenv-configured uv binary.

  Debug:
    version           Show appenv version.
    settings          Show environment variables and settings.
    profiling         Manage profiling data.
```

### init

Create a new project with `pyproject.toml`:

```text
$ ./appenv init
Let's create a new pyproject.toml project.

What should the command be named? [app] mycli
Enter dependencies (one per line, empty line to finish):
  Default: mycli
  Dependency: click
  Dependency: rich
  Dependency:
Project name [mycli-app]:
Description []: My awesome CLI
Minimum Python version [3.10]: 3.14

Created pyproject.toml
```

If `pyproject.toml` already exists:

```text
$ ./appenv init
pyproject.toml already exists in /path/to/project.
Nothing to do.
Edit pyproject.toml manually to make changes.
```

### migrate

Convert an existing `requirements.txt` project to `pyproject.toml`. See [Migrating from requirements.txt](#migrating-from-requirementstxt) for details.

### update-lockfile

Generate or update `uv.lock`:

```text
$ ./appenv update-lockfile          # Update lockfile
$ ./appenv update-lockfile --diff   # Show changes without writing
$ ./appenv update-lockfile -v       # Verbose output
```

### reset

Remove the virtual environment and clean up legacy artifacts:

```text
$ ./appenv reset
Removing .venv symlink ...
Removing .appenv/venv ...
```

Also removes old `.venv` directory (if not a symlink) and cleans up old hash-based venvs from previous appenv versions. Preserves logs and profiling data.

### prepare

Create the virtual environment and install production dependencies only.

Uses `uv sync --no-dev --frozen` - requires an existing `uv.lock` and will not modify it.
Called automatically when running the application via the symlink.

### develop

Create the virtual environment with dev dependencies (from `[dependency-groups] dev`):

```text
$ ./appenv develop
```

Uses `uv sync` without `--frozen`, so the lockfile may be updated if `pyproject.toml` has changed. Useful for development when you need tools like pytest, ruff, etc.

### python

Start a Python REPL in the virtual environment:

```text
$ ./appenv python
Python 3.11.0 (main, ...)
>>>
```

### run

Run a script from the venv's bin directory:

```text
$ ./appenv run pytest
```

### uv

Run uv with appenv's configured environment:

```text
$ ./appenv uv add requests            # Add dependency (updates pyproject.toml + uv.lock)
$ ./appenv uv add --group dev pytest  # Add dev dependency
$ ./appenv uv remove requests         # Remove dependency
$ ./appenv uv lock --upgrade          # Upgrade all packages in lockfile
$ ./appenv uv sync                    # Re-sync dependencies
```

### settings

Show environment variables and settings:

```text
$ ./appenv settings
appenv environment:

  APPENV_EXTRAS: (not set)
  APPENV_VERBOSE: (not set)
  APPENV_PROFILE: (not set)
  ...
```

See {doc}`workflows` for detailed output example.

### profiling

Manage profiling data:

```text
$ ./appenv profiling list              # List recent profiles
$ ./appenv profiling show              # Show latest profile with pstats
$ ./appenv profiling show file.prof    # Show specific profile
$ ./appenv profiling snakeviz          # Open latest profile in snakeviz
```

Enable profiling with `APPENV_PROFILE=1`. See {doc}`workflows` for detailed examples.

## Environment Variables

- `APPENV_VERBOSE=1` - Show verbose output during bootstrap
- `APPENV_EXTRAS` - Extras to install (comma-separated)
- `APPENV_PROFILE=1` - Enable profiling
- `APPENV_BASEDIR` - Base directory of the project
- `APPENV_BEST_PYTHON` - Selected Python interpreter

See {doc}`workflows` for verbose mode details.

## Requirements

- Python 3.10+
- uv 0.5.0+ (auto-installed if not found)

## Testing

If you want to contribute, please install `tox` and run it.

```text
$ tox
```
